00 45         # errorCode = 69
00 00 00 00   # throttleTimeMs = 0
00 00 00 00   # topics: 0 item(s)
```

### `heartbeat.response.v3.fenced-instance-id`

The answer: the error code **82** (`FencedInstanceId`). The older consumer is fenced for good - its heartbeats, its commits and its syncs are answered 82 from here on, and only a new `group.instance.id` or the other consumer leaving frees the identity again.

### `groupcoordinator.request.v3`

FindCoordinator request v3 (Kafka 2.4, KIP-482), the first **flexible** frame of the group apis: the header is the request header **v2** and ends in a tagged-field section, the group id is a `compact_string` whose length is the unsigned varint `20 + 1`, and the body closes with a tag buffer of its own. The `client_id` of the header stays an `int16`-prefixed string in every version - `"flexibleVersions": "none"` in `RequestHeader.json` @ 2.8.2.

<!-- vector: groupcoordinator.request.v3 -->
```
00 00 00 35                                       # messageSize = 53
00 0a                                             # apiKey = 10
00 03                                             # apiVersion = 3
00 00 03 85                                       # correlationId = 901
00 13 6b 61 66 6b 61 2d 63 6c 69 65 6e 74 2d 74   # clientId = "kafka-client-t3-24b" (int16 length, never compact)
33 2d 32 34 62
00                                                # TAG_BUFFER of the request header v2: no tagged field
15 74 33 2d 32 34 62 2d 76 65 63 74 6f 72 73 2d   # consumerGroup = "t3-24b-vectors-group" (compact: 20 + 1)
67 72 6f 75 70
00                                                # coordinatorType = 0
00                                                # TAG_BUFFER of the body: no tagged field
```

### `groupcoordinator.response.v3`

The answer: the response header **v1**, whose tag buffer follows the correlation id, and the four fields of the version 1 answer in the compact encoding. The `node_id`, `host` and `port` of the coordinator are three ordinary fields of the answer and **not** a structure of their own, so the frame carries exactly one more tag buffer - the one that closes the body.

<!-- vector: groupcoordinator.response.v3 -->
```

00 00 03 85                     # correlationId = 901
00                              # TAG_BUFFER of the response header v1: no tagged field
00 00 00 00                     # throttleTimeMs = 0
00 00                           # errorCode = 0
05 4e 4f 4e 45                  # errorMessage = "NONE" (compact: 4 + 1)
00 00 00 00                     # coordinator.nodeId = 0
0a 31 32 37 2e 30 2e 30 2e 31   # coordinator.host = "127.0.0.1" (compact: 9 + 1)
00 00 23 84                     # coordinator.port = 9092
00                              # TAG_BUFFER of the body: no tagged field
```

### `metadata.request.v9`

Metadata request v9 (Kafka 2.4), the first FLEXIBLE version of this api (KIP-482): the request header v2 - the client id as a NON-compact string and a tag buffer of its own behind it - a COMPACT topic array (the unsigned varint 02 for one entry), the topic name as a compact string (0b for ten bytes), the three booleans of the versions 4 and 8 and the tagged-field section of the body. The question is the one of version 8, in the other encoding.

<!-- vector: metadata.request.v9 -->
```
00 00 00 1e                        # messageSize = 30
00 03                              # apiKey = 3
00 09                              # apiVersion = 9
00 00 02 58                        # correlationId = 600
00 02 74 32                        # clientId = "t2" (int16 length, never compact)
00                                 # TAG_BUFFER of the request header v2: no tagged field
02                                 # topics: 1 item(s) (compact: 1 + 1)
0b 74 32 2d 32 34 2d 66 6c 65 78   # topics[0].name = "t2-24-flex" (compact: 10 + 1)
00                                 # TAG_BUFFER of the structure topics[0]: no tagged field
00                                 # allowAutoTopicCreation = false
00                                 # includeClusterAuthorizedOperations = false
00                                 # includeTopicAuthorizedOperations = false
00                                 # TAG_BUFFER of the body: no tagged field
```

### `createtopics.request.v4`

CreateTopics request v4, the frame KIP-464 gave a new meaning in Kafka 2.4: `num_partitions` and `replication_factor` are both -1 and the assignment array is EMPTY, which asks the broker for its own `num.partitions` and `default.replication.factor`. The bytes are those of a version 3 request with another version field; what the version 4 buys is that a broker of Kafka 2.3 or below will not silently refuse the -1.

<!-- vector: createtopics.request.v4 -->
```
00 00 00 3a                                    # messageSize = 58
00 13                                          # apiKey = 19
00 04                                          # apiVersion = 4
00 00 03 e9                                    # correlationId = 1001
00 0a 74 34 2d 76 65 63 74 6f 72 73            # clientId = "t4-vectors"
00 00 00 01                                    # topics: 1 item(s)
00 0d 74 34 2d 32 34 2d 76 65 63 74 6f 72 73   # topics[t4-24-vectors].topic = "t4-24-vectors"
ff ff ff ff                                    # topics[t4-24-vectors].numPartitions = -1
ff ff                                          # topics[t4-24-vectors].replicationFactor = -1
00 00 00 00                                    # topics[t4-24-vectors].replicaAssignment: 0 item(s)
00 00 00 00                                    # topics[t4-24-vectors].configs: 0 item(s)
00 00 75 30                                    # timeout = 30000
00                                             # validateOnly = false
```

### `electleaders.response.v1.unclean`

The answer for it: the top-level error code 0 - the request reached the controller - and the same 84 per partition. `KafkaController.processReplicaLeaderElection` @ 2.8.2 only elects unclean for a partition whose leader is GONE (`currentLeader == LeaderAndIsr.NoLeader || !liveBrokerIds.contains(currentLeader)`), so a partition that still has a live leader needs no election of either kind.

### `describeclientquotas.request.v0`

DescribeClientQuotas request v0 for one named `client-id`. Kafka 2.6 added this api **after** KIP-482 and still without the compact encoding - `DescribeClientQuotasRequest.json` @ 2.6.3 and @ 2.7.2 both say `"flexibleVersions": "none"` - so the frame is a plain one: int16-prefixed strings, an int32-counted component array and no tag buffer anywhere. `strict` is the single byte `00` that closes it.

<!-- vector: describeclientquotas.request.v0 -->
```
00 00 00 44                                       # messageSize = 68
00 30                                             # apiKey = 48
00 00                                             # apiVersion = 0
00 00 17 d6                                       # correlationId = 6102
00 17 6b 61 66 6b 61 2d 63 6c 69 65 6e 74 2d 74   # clientId = "kafka-client-t1-vectors"
31 2d 76 65 63 74 6f 72 73
00 00 00 01                                       # components: 1 item(s)
00 09 63 6c 69 65 6e 74 2d 69 64                  # components[0].entityType = "client-id"
00                                                # components[0].matchType = 0
00 10 74 31 2d 71 75 6f 74 61 2d 76 65 63 74 6f   # components[0].match = "t1-quota-vectors"
72 73
00                                                # strict = false
```

### `describeclientquotas.response.v0`

The answer of the container: one entry, whose entity is the array `[client-id = t1-quota-vectors]` and whose values are the two quotas that were set. **`producer_byte_rate` and `request_percentage` are `float64`s** - eight bytes of an IEEE 754 double in network order, `41 30 00 00 00 00 00 00` being 1048576 and `40 29 00 00 00 00 00 00` being 12.5 - the only place in this protocol where that type appears.

<!-- vector: describeclientquotas.response.v0 -->
```
00 00 00 6d                                       # messageSize = 109
00 00 17 d6                                       # correlationId = 6102
00 00 00 00                                       # throttleTimeMs = 0
00 00                                             # errorCode = 0
00 00                                             # errorMessage = ""

00 10 74 31 2d 71 75 6f 74 61 2d 76 65 63 74 6f   # entries[0].entity[client-id].entityName = "t1-quota-vectors"
72 73
00 00 00 02                                       # entries[0].values: 2 item(s)
00 12 72 65 71 75 65 73 74 5f 70 65 72 63 65 6e   # entries[0].values[request_percentage].key = "request_percentage"
74 61 67 65
40 29 00 00 00 00 00 00                           # entries[0].values[request_percentage].value = 12.5
00 12 70 72 6f 64 75 63 65 72 5f 62 79 74 65 5f   # entries[0].values[producer_byte_rate].key = "producer_byte_rate"
72 61 74 65
41 30 00 00 00 00 00 00                           # entries[0].values[producer_byte_rate].value = 1048576

### `describeclientquotas.response.v0.unsupported-entity-type`

What a filter for an entity type the broker does not know is answered with: **35** (`UnsupportedVersion`, not 42) and the message *"Custom entity type 't1-nonsense' not supported"*, and the entry array is **null** (`ff ff ff ff`) - `DescribeClientQuotasResponse.fromException()` @ 2.8.2 builds every error answer with a null array, while a filter that simply matched nothing answers an empty one.

<!-- vector: describeclientquotas.response.v0.unsupported-entity-type -->
```
00 00 00 3e                                       # messageSize = 62
00 00 17 d8                                       # correlationId = 6104
00 00 00 00                                       # throttleTimeMs = 0
00 23                                             # errorCode = 35
00 2e 43 75 73 74 6f 6d 20 65 6e 74 69 74 79 20   # errorMessage = "Custom entity type 't1-nonsense' not supported"
74 79 70 65 20 27 74 31 2d 6e 6f 6e 73 65 6e 73
65 27 20 6e 6f 74 20 73 75 70 70 6f 72 74 65 64
ff ff ff ff                                       # entries: null
```

### `describeclientquotas.response.v0.unknown-match-type`

And what a **match type** the broker does not know is answered with: the error code **-1** (`UnknownServerError`) and a null message. `DescribeClientQuotasRequest.filter()` @ 2.8.2 throws a plain `IllegalArgumentException("Unexpected match type: 7")` before any error mapping happens, so the request falls into the generic handler of `KafkaApis` - a validation gap of the broker rather than a code it means to send.

<!-- vector: describeclientquotas.response.v0.unknown-match-type -->
```
00 00 00 10   # messageSize = 16
00 00 17 d9   # correlationId = 6105
00 00 00 00   # throttleTimeMs = 0
ff ff         # errorCode = -1
ff ff         # errorMessage = null
ff ff ff ff   # entries: null
```

### `alterclientquotas.request.v0`

AlterClientQuotas request v0 that sets two quotas of one `client-id`. Every op carries its `float64` value **and** the `remove` flag, because the frame has no optional fields: a set is the value with `00`, a removal a value the broker ignores with `01`. The last byte is `validate_only`.

ListGroups request v4 (Kafka 2.6, KIP-518): the first frame of this api with a field of its own, the `states_filter` - here one entry, `Stable`, as a compact array of compact strings. ### `listgroups.request.v4.unknown-state`

The same request with the state `stable` in lower case. `GroupCoordinator.handleListGroups` @ 2.8.2 compares the names with `states.contains(g.summary.state)`, a plain string comparison, so the filter is **case sensitive** and a name that is not a state is not an error.

### `fetch.response.v12.diverging-epoch`

The answer to that fetch: the leader compares the stated epoch and offset with its own log, finds that the two diverge and answers the TAGGED field 0 diverging_epoch - the largest epoch from which the logs are known to differ (0) and the offset it ends at (1) - with an EMPTY record set, the error code 0 and the real high water mark. The fetcher truncates to that offset and carries on, which is the truncation detection of KIP-320 done inside the fetch itself. It is also the one tagged field of this api that a ZooKeeper-backed broker ever fills in: the tag 0 with its own length, count and structure, and the partition ends without the tags 1 and 2.

### `describeuserscramcredentials.request.v0`

DescribeUserScramCredentials request v0 for one user. The api is **flexible from its version 0** - Kafka 2.7 is well past KIP-482 - so the request header v2, a compact user array whose entries are structures of one compact string, and a tag buffer after the entry and after the body. A **null** user array (the single byte `00`) and an **empty** one (`01`) both mean "every user that has a credential", which the specification says in as many words.

### `alteruserscramcredentials.request.v0`

EndTxn answer v2: the error code 0 - the coordinator took the decision and writes the markers afterwards.

<!-- vector: endtxn.response.v2 -->
```
00 00 00 0a   # messageSize = 10
00 00 03 c7   # correlationId = 967
00 00 00 00   # throttleTimeMs = 0
00 00         # errorCode = 0
```

### `endtxn.response.v2.fenced`

EndTxn answer v2 to a producer that a later incarnation of the same transactional id has fenced: the error code **90** `ProducerFenced` of KIP-588, where the versions 0 and 1 are answered the 47.

<!-- vector: endtxn.response.v2.fenced -->
```
00 00 00 0a   # messageSize = 10
00 00 03 c9   # correlationId = 969
00 00 00 00   # throttleTimeMs = 0
00 5a         # errorCode = 90
```
